chief_complaint: severe burning pain, swelling, shiny discolored skin, and joint stiffness in hand 8 weeks after distal radius fracture (Complex Regional Pain Syndrome CRPS)
hpi_details: 58F presents to pain rehabilitation clinic 8 weeks after suffering a right distal radius fracture (Colles fracture) that was treated with closed reduction and a plaster cast for 6 weeks. When the cast was removed 2 weeks ago, her right hand and fingers were exquisitely painful, burning constantly, severely swollen, and stiff. Pain is a 9/10 burning sensation that is triggered agonizingly merely by blowing cool air on the hand or touching it with a soft shirt sleeve (allodynia). Hand turns alternately dusky mottled blue and bright angry red, feels colder than the left hand, and shows shiny, tight skin with rapid hair and nail growth.
ideas: in agonizing burning discomfort holding her right hand carefully against her chest to prevent anyone from touching it
concerns: terrified her hand is permanently damaged or dying off due to the dark blue color changes
expectations: wants immediate nerve pain treatment and specialized physical therapy to stop the burning and swelling
social_hx: Real estate agent, right-hand dominant, non-smoker

clinical_knowledge.topic: Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Complex Regional Pain Syndrome is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes a multidisciplinary aggressive functional rehabilitation protocol with desensitization therapy and graded motor imagery, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: severe burning pain, swelling, shiny discolored skin, and joint stiffness in hand 8 weeks after distal radius fracture (Complex Regional Pain Syndrome CRPS)

Key HPI features: 58F presents to pain rehabilitation clinic 8 weeks after suffering a right distal radius fracture (Colles fracture) that was treated with closed reduction and a plaster cast for 6 weeks. When the cast was removed 2 weeks ago, her right hand and fingers were exquisitely painful, burning constantly, severely swollen, and stiff. Pain is a 9/10 burning sensation that is triggered agonizingly merely by blowing cool air on the hand or touching it with a soft shirt sleeve (allodynia). Hand turns alternately dusky mottled blue and bright angry red, feels colder than the left hand, and shows shiny, tight skin with rapid hair and nail growth.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 76, BP 130/80. Right upper extremity exam reveals marked diffuse non-pitting edema over the dorsum of the right hand and digits. Skin over the fingers is glossy, shiny, tight, and demonstrates mottled cyanotic/erythematous vasomotor discoloration. Infrared surface thermometry confirms the right hand is 2.4C colder than the contralateral normal left hand (vasomotor instability). Hyperhidrosis (sweating) present over right palm. Exquisite mechanical ALLODYNIA elicited by light touch with a cotton swab across the dorsal hand and fingers. Active and passive range of motion across all right metacarpophalangeal (MCP) and interphalangeal (IP) joints is severely restricted by pain and edema. Right wrist X-ray shows healed distal radius fracture with prominent, patchy, periarticular osteopenia ('Sudeck atrophy').
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Complex Regional Pain Syndrome.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Soft tissue strain or simple post-immobilization stiffness without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: signs of limb-threatening vascular compromise or an undiagnosed fracture/infection mimicking CRPS.
management_principles: Multidisciplinary PM&R aggressive functional rehabilitation protocol: combine desensitization therapy, edema control, and active range of motion with graded motor imagery/mirror box therapy.

Physical/Occupational Therapy (FOUNDATIONAL PILLAR): initiate immediate gentle, progressive desensitization therapy (systematically rubbing the skin with silk, cotton, and towel textures), contrast baths, edema control (compression glove), and active range of motion exercises
Refer to Graded Motor Imagery (GMI) and Mirror Box Therapy to reorganize maladaptive cortical representations
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 58F presenting with disproportionate burning neuropathic pain, mechanical allodynia, vasomotor instability, sudomotor changes, and trophic skin changes following immobilization of a distal radius fracture, meeting Budapest consensus criteria for Complex Regional Pain Syndrome.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: HR 76, BP 130/80. Right upper extremity exam reveals marked diffuse non-pitting edema over the dorsum of the right hand and digits. Skin over the fingers is glossy, shiny, tight, and demonstrates mottled cyanotic/erythematous vasomotor discoloration. Infrared surface thermometry confirms the right hand is 2.4C colder than the contralateral normal left hand (vasomotor instability). Hyperhidrosis (sweating) present over right palm. Exquisite mechanical ALLODYNIA elicited by light touch with a cotton swab across the dorsal hand and fingers. Active and passive range of motion across all right metacarpophalangeal (MCP) and interphalangeal (IP) joints is severely restricted by pain and edema. Right wrist X-ray shows healed distal radius fracture with prominent, patchy, periarticular osteopenia ('Sudeck atrophy').
reference_soap.assessment: Complex Regional Pain Syndrome Type I (CRPS Type I / Reflex Sympathetic Dystrophy RSD) of the Right Upper Extremity, meeting clinical Budapest Criteria.
reference_soap.plan: First reassess for an unhealed fracture, infection, vascular compromise, or another diagnosis requiring urgent treatment. When CRPS is clinically confirmed, use gentle, function-focused physical and occupational therapy with pacing, desensitization, edema management, and active range of motion; avoid forcing painful movement. Neuropathic agents, corticosteroids, bisphosphonates, sympathetic blocks, and neuromodulation require individualized risk-benefit review and pain/rehabilitation specialist involvement, particularly when pain prevents function despite conservative care.

learning_objectives: Apply the clinical Budapest Diagnostic Criteria for Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS: continuing pain disproportionate to inciting event, plus >=1 symptom and >=1 sign across Sensory [allodynia/hyperalgesia], Vasomotor [temperature/color asymmetry >1C], Sudomotor/Edema [sweating/swelling], and Motor/Trophic [stiffness/hair/nail changes] categories)

Differentiate CRPS Type I (Reflex Sympathetic Dystrophy occurring without documented major peripheral nerve injury following fractures/casts) from CRPS Type II (Causalgia occurring after confirmed distinct peripheral nerve trunk transection/injury)

Prioritize foundational functional rehabilitation utilizing Graded Motor Imagery, Mirror Box Therapy, and tactile desensitization to reverse cortical somatosensory reorganization over passive immobility

Outline interventional pain management escalation from sympathetic nerve blocks (Stellate Ganglion block for upper extremity, Lumbar Sympathetic block for lower extremity) to neuromodulation (Spinal Cord Stimulation)

teaching.one_liner: Disproportionate burning neuropathic pain, allodynia, and vasomotor/trophic changes in a limb following injury or immobilization.
red_flags: Signs of vascular compromise (absent pulses, cold pale limb) rather than CRPS vasomotor changes
Fever or purulence suggesting infection rather than CRPS
Undiagnosed fracture or compartment syndrome mimicking CRPS pain

must_ask.say: When did this pain start compared to your fracture and the time your cast was removed?
Is the pain a burning sensation, and does it get triggered by something as light as air or fabric touching your skin?
Have you noticed your hand changing color, like turning blue or red, or feeling colder than the other side?
Has the hand been swollen, or have you noticed changes in your skin, hair, or nail growth?
How much is this affecting your ability to move or use your hand for daily tasks?
